findings.title: isinstance check never matches spawn processes, so hung or dead flushers are never killed
findings.body: The processes are created from `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, so they are `SpawnProcess` instances. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False. The kill is therefore skipped on every restart. A hung flusher keeps running, and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second process for the same shards. Duplicate flushers can then produce duplicate or fragmented segments. The old code called `kill()` unconditionally and only caught ValueError. The same check in `join()` (around line 346) means spawned children are never terminated at shutdown.

findings.title: join() never terminates spawned flusher processes
findings.body: The `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard in `join()` is False for `SpawnProcess` objects, so `terminate()` is never called. Processes that did not exit before the deadline keep running after the consumer shuts down. The early `break` on an expired deadline also skips the remaining processes entirely.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep
findings.body: The test patches `time.sleep` to a lambda at the top, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)` returns immediately. The comment says it gives flusher threads time to process after the drift change, but it does not. The test can call `step.join()` before the flusher has produced anything, making `(msg,) = messages` flaky.

findings.title: --flusher-processes defaults to 1, contradicting the one-process-per-shard intent
findings.body: The PR's goal is one flusher process per Redis shard. The CLI option defaults to 1, so existing deployments get a single flusher for all shards unless they change the flag. The help text says 'Defaults to 1', but the factory treats None as one process per shard. The CLI default should be None, or the behaviour should match the description.

findings.title: Unused _create_process_for_shard restarts a process without terminating the old one
findings.body: This helper is never called. If it were, it would start a new process for the shard's group without killing or joining the existing one, which leaks the old process. It should be removed or fixed.

findings.title: New flusher_processes parameter inserted before produce_to_pipe breaks positional callers
findings.body: `flusher_processes` was placed before `produce_to_pipe` in the constructor signature. Any caller that passes `produce_to_pipe` positionally will now pass it into `flusher_processes`. Adding the new parameter at the end, or making it keyword-only, avoids this.
